question: The marked price of an article is ₹360. The shopkeeper offers a discount of 11% on the purchase of the article. Thereby, he makes a profit of 20%. The cost price of the article is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

We know the direct relationship between CP and MP:

CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 + Profit%)

⇒ CP ÷ 360 = (100 − 11) ÷ (100 + 20)

⇒ CP = 360 × (89 ÷ 120)

⇒ CP = 3 × 89 = 267

**∴ The correct answer is ₹267.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹360

Discount = 11%

Profit = 20%

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 CP = ?
 
 
• 
 +20%
 
 
 SP = 320.4
 
 
• 
 −11%
 
 
 MP = 360
 
 CP = 320.4 ÷ 1.2 = ₹267

**Calculations:**

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

⇒ SP = 360 × (100 − 11) ÷ 100 = 360 × 89 ÷ 100 = ₹320.4

Now, calculating Cost Price (CP) from SP and Profit%:

⇒ SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100

⇒ 320.4 = CP × (100 + 20) ÷ 100

⇒ CP = 320.4 × 100 ÷ 120

⇒ CP = 3204 ÷ 12 = 267

**∴ The correct answer is ₹267.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Relation Formula

The ratio of Cost Price to Marked Price is directly given by: CP / MP = (100 − D%) / (100 + P%).

Successive Discounts

The single equivalent discount for two successive discounts d₁% and d₂% is calculated as: d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂) / 100.

Markup Percentage

It represents how much the Marked Price is set above the Cost Price: Markup% = (MP − CP) / CP × 100.
